result.markdown: --- title: "07 · ANOVA as a linear model" subtitle: "Week 2" --- ::: {.guiding-q} And what about ANOVA? ::: ## In this session - One-way ANOVA = linear model with one categorical predictor (session 04 revisited) - Factorial ANOVA = categorical predictors with interactions (session 05 revisited) - *F*-tests as comparisons between nested models - Types of sums of squares (I, II, III) and why the order of terms can matter - Repeated measures: a first look at non-independence (prepares session 11) ::: {.key-terms} **Key terms:** [Contrasts and dummy coding](../../glossary.qmd#contrasts), [Degrees of freedom](../../glossary.qmd#df) ::: ## Learning goals After this session you can - reproduce an ANOVA table from a linear model, - explain an *F*-test as a comparison of a full and a reduced model, - choose an appropriate type of sums of squares for unbalanced data. ## Simulate first ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(7) group <- factor(rep(c("control", "food", "toy"), each = 20)) y <- rnorm(60, c(control = 10, food = 14, toy = 12)[group], 3) summary(aov(y ~ group)) # classic one-way ANOVA ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F) #> group 2 91.2 45.59 5.186 0.00853 ** #> Residuals 57 501.1 8.79 #> --- #> Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} full <- lm(y ~ group) null <- lm(y ~ 1) anova(null, full) # same F: a comparison of two models ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> Analysis of Variance Table #> #> Model 1: y ~ 1 #> Model 2: y ~ group #> Res.Df RSS Df Sum of Sq F Pr(>F) #> 1 59 592.30 #> 2 57 501.12 2 91.179 5.1856 0.00853 ** #> --- #> Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 ``` ::: ::: ## Materials ::: {.materials} - Slides coming soon - R script coming soon - Exercises coming soon ::: ## Reading - Fox (2016), ch. 8. - Lindeløv (2019), see [session 06](06-t-test.qmd).
